explanation: Conditional compilation in C allows specific parts of the code to be included or excluded during preprocessing based on whether certain macros are defined. It is used to create platform-specific code, ensuring that programs can adapt to different operating systems like FreeBSD, Linux, or Mac OS X, which helps in maintaining portability and avoiding compilation errors on unsupported platforms.

extraction_metadata.source: Advanced Programming in the UNIX Environment 3rd Edition

book: Advanced Programming in the UNIX Environment (3rd Edition)
code_example:
#if defined(__FreeBSD__)
#define OS_ID 1
#define SYS_API "kqueue"
void freebsd_setup();
#elif defined(__linux__)
#define OS_ID 2
#define SYS_API "epoll"
void linux_setup();
#elif defined(__APPLE__)
#define OS_ID 3
#define SYS_API "kqueue"
void macos_setup();
#else
#define OS_ID 0
#define SYS_API "none"
#error "Platform not supported."
#endif

// OS_ID is now defined based on the detected OS.
keywords: #if defined, conditional compilation, #ifdef, C preprocessor directives
